metadata.name: Ecodesign for Scala
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Scala code: lazy transformations, bounded parallelism, no needless materialisation.

collections.name: Scala — collections and evaluation
collections.description: Do not materialise what you only traverse once (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Chained transformations materialised at each step
rules.description: Every map or filter on a strict collection allocates a new one. Three links in the chain over a large collection means three full copies for a single result.
rules.recommendation: Use .iterator or .view for the chain and materialise only the final result. On a small collection the strict version stays clearer.
rules.note: A single .view or .iterator anywhere in the file silences the rule. On a short collection the strict chain costs less than the indirection, so the volume is what settles it.

rules.title: Parallel collection without measurement
rules.description: .par hands the work to a shared pool for a gain that is rarely measured, and it degrades every other task sharing that pool.
rules.recommendation: Stay sequential by default. Parallelise only after a benchmark, on a pool you sized yourself.

rules.title: Future built eagerly in a loop
rules.description: A Future starts as soon as it is constructed. Building them inside a loop launches every call at once, with no bound on how many run in parallel.
rules.recommendation: Bound the concurrency explicitly, with a throttled traverse or a semaphore, so the number in flight stays a decision rather than a consequence of the list length.
rules.note: One Semaphore, parTraverseN or throttle anywhere in the file silences the rule. A Future built over a list of known, small length is bounded by construction.
